title: Where, for a Thousand Miles
description: Where, for a Thousand Miles in Tonic Solfa to DORT, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 417, “"How Beautiful upon the Mountains."”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sixes and Fours (6.6.4.6.6.6.4) (6.6.4.6.6.6.4), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DORT; any other Sixes and Fours (6.6.4.6.6.6.4) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Where, for a thou-sand miles, The sweet O-hi-o smiles, On bed of sand; Where prai-ries blos-som broad, Fair gar-dens sown by God, And lakes their o-cean flood Pour from His hand;

lines: From heart to heart shall reach
The feet of those who bear
O Thou, whose suns and rains
Send down the dews of peace,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to DORT by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
